input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Use atomic writes in CacheStore to prevent corruption

CacheStore.store() previously wrote content and metadata in two
separate fs::write calls. If concurrent tool installations targeted
the same cache key, or the process was interrupted between the two
writes, content and metadata could become inconsistent — e.g. new
content with old metadata reporting the wrong size.

Both store() and save_metadata() now write to NamedTempFile in the
same directory, then persist (rename) atomically. rename(2) is atomic
on the same filesystem, so readers always see either the complete old
entry or the complete new entry, never a half-written state.

tempfile is promoted from dev-dependency to regular dependency to
support NamedTempFile::persist at runtime.
EOF
)"

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Use atomic writes in CacheStore to prevent corruption

CacheStore.store() previously wrote content and metadata in two
separate fs::write calls. If concurrent tool installations targeted
the same cache key, or the process was interrupted between the two
writes, content and metadata could become inconsistent — e.g. new
content with old metadata reporting the wrong size.

Both store() and save_metadata() now write to NamedTempFile in the
same directory, then persist (rename) atomically. rename(2) is atomic
on the same filesystem, so readers always see either the complete old
entry or the complete new entry, never a half-written state.

tempfile is promoted from dev-dependency to regular dependency to
support NamedTempFile::persist at runtime.
EOF
)"

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Use atomic writes in CacheStore to prevent corruption

CacheStore.store() previously wrote content and metadata in two
separate fs::write calls. If concurrent tool installations targeted
the same cache key, or the process was interrupted between the two
writes, content and metadata could become inconsistent — e.g. new
content with old metadata reporting the wrong size.

Both store() and save_metadata() now write to NamedTempFile in the
same directory, then persist (rename) atomically. rename(2) is atomic
on the same filesystem, so readers always see either the complete old
entry or the complete new entry, never a half-written state.

tempfile is promoted from dev-dependency to regular dependency to
support NamedTempFile::persist at runtime.
EOF
)"

content.content:
commit 62c71492e8c80aee7398fa51f95764a97d992236
Author: benchmark <benchmark@localhost>
Date:   Sun Mar 15 17:38:31 2026 -0600

    Use atomic writes in CacheStore to prevent corruption
    
    CacheStore.store() previously wrote content and metadata in two
    separate fs::write calls. If concurrent tool installations targeted
    the same cache key, or the process was interrupted between the two
    writes, content and metadata could become inconsistent — e.g. new
    content with old metadata reporting the wrong size.
    
    Both store() and save_metadata() now write to NamedTempFile in the
    same directory, then persist (rename) atomically. rename(2) is atomic
    on the same filesystem, so readers always see either the complete old
    entry or the complete new entry, never a half-written state.
    
    tempfile is promoted from dev-dependency to regular dependency to
    support NamedTempFile::persist at runtime.
